parsed.title: Which Scholars Accept the Facts for the Resurrection? - Gary Habermas
parsed.summary: This is a YouTube interview chapter in which Gary Habermas defends the 'minimal facts' method for the resurrection against the objection that scholarly consensus is merely a Christian-bias artifact. He argues that even hostile/liberal scholars (Bultmann, the Jesus Seminar, Antony Flew) concede key facts, and he lays out criteria for counting a 'critical scholar' (terminal degree plus field competence/publication). The material is almost entirely historical-apologetic and evidentiary; it touches the axiom system only at the periphery, chiefly by presupposing that testimony/evidence can be assessed by informed observers and by treating the resurrection as a factual claim about a terminal divine act. It does not engage the physics-theology formal apparatus (chi field, master equation, coherence functionals, etc.).

axiom_nodes.name: A5.1 — Observation Requirement
axiom_nodes.notes: The whole discussion turns on who counts as a qualified observer/witness of the evidence (terminal degree, field competence), which is conceptually adjacent to an observation requirement, but no claim about observation as an ontological requirement is made.

axiom_nodes.name: BC1 — Terminal Observer Exists
axiom_nodes.notes: The resurrection is treated as a divine act terminating the causal chain of testimony, but the transcript never formulates a terminal-observer axiom.

axiom_nodes.name: ID7.1 — Terminal Observer Is God
axiom_nodes.notes: God is implicitly the agent behind the resurrection, but the identification of a terminal observer with God is not asserted.

axiom_nodes.name: PERSONHOOD — Agency, Intentionality, Relational Capacity
axiom_nodes.evidence_quote: The earliest disciples preached that he was raised from the dead.
axiom_nodes.notes: The discussion presupposes personal agency (disciples preaching, scholars reasoning, God acting) without theorizing it.

axiom_nodes.name: A11.1 — Moral Realism
axiom_nodes.notes: Habermas appeals to scholarly honesty and fairness ('they're being honest to the data'), which gestures at normative epistemic/moral standards, but no moral-realism axiom is stated.

axiom_nodes.name: A4.1 — Parsimony
axiom_nodes.notes: The minimal-facts method is a parsimony-style move (fewest contested claims), but parsimony is not invoked as a formal axiom.

axiom_nodes.name: EV15.1 — Biblical Prophecy Validation
axiom_nodes.notes: The chapter is historical-evidential about the resurrection, not about prophecy validation specifically.
